merger_description:
Danfoss A/S (**Danfoss**) proposes to acquire sole control of Alfa Gomma S.p.A. in liquidazione (**Alfagomma**) (with the exception of certain assets) by way of a share purchase agreement (the **Acquisition**).

Danfoss is a family and foundation owned limited liability company established in Denmark, controlled by the Bitten & Mads Clausen’s Foundation. Danfoss operates globally, with sales in more than 100 countries. Danfoss is active in the development, manufacturing and distribution of components and engineering technologies for refrigeration, heating, air conditioning, industrial automation, hydraulics, high-pressure systems and frequency converters. Danfoss also provides solutions for renewable energy and district energy infrastructure. Relevant to the Acquisition, Danfoss offers fluid conveyance products including hydraulic hoses, industrial hoses, fittings, adapters and assemblies.

Alfagomma is established in Italy and is a global manufacturer and distributor of fluid handling systems for hydraulic and industrial applications. Alfagomma operates across two main business areas: high-pressure hoses, hydraulic hoses, manipulated tubes, fittings and adapters and rubber industrial hoses, PVC industrial pipes and industrial tubes made of thermoplastic rubber. Alfagomma is currently undergoing voluntary liquidation. A board of receivers was appointed by the Court of Milan on 27 May 2025 with authority to identify and pursue strategic alternatives and operational measures deemed appropriate to ensure stable ongoing operations and to protect the value of Alfagomma’s business.

Danfoss and Alfagomma overlap in the supply of hydraulic hoses and fittings and industrial hoses and fittings.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, publicly available information and information
received from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• Danfoss and Alfagomma are not close competitors in the supply
of industrial and hydraulic hoses and fittings in Australia.
• The merged firm would continue to face competition from
multiple alternative suppliers of industrial and hydraulic hoses
and fittings.
• The merged firm is unlikely to have the ability and incentive to
foreclose rival suppliers that currently use Danfoss products due
to the availability of alternative suppliers of these products.
